sanskrit: sa naḥ prakṣyati sarveṣu kāryeṣv arthaviniścayam tatra buddhiṃ pravakṣyāmo yathā yajño nivartate
english: He will ask us to determine the purpose in all matters; there we shall offer our counsel so that the sacrifice may be averted.

sanskrit: sa no bahumatān rājā buddhvā buddhimatāṃ varaḥ yajñārthaṃ prakṣyati vyaktaṃ neti vakṣyāmahe vayam
english: Knowing us, who are well esteemed, to be the best among the wise, that king will clearly ask us for the sake of the sacrifice — and we shall say: no.

sanskrit: darśayanto bahūn doṣān pretya ceha ca dāruṇān hetubhiḥ kāraṇaiś caiva yathā yajño bhaven na saḥ
english: Showing many terrible faults pertaining to the next world and to this one, with reasons and grounds, we shall argue that the sacrifice should not take place.

sanskrit: athavā ya upādhyāyaḥ kratau tasmin bhaviṣyati sarpasatravidhānajño rājakāryahite rataḥ
english: Or, whoever shall be the officiating priest at that rite — one who knows the ritual procedure of the serpent sacrifice and is devoted to serving the king's interest —

sanskrit: taṃ gatvā daśatāṃ kaś cid bhujagaḥ sa mariṣyati tasmin hate yajñakare kratuḥ sa na bhaviṣyati
english: Let some serpent go and bite him; he shall die. When that performer of the sacrifice is slain, the rite shall not proceed.

sanskrit: ye cānye sarpasatrajñā bhaviṣyanty asya ṛtvijaḥ tāṃś ca sarvān daśiṣyāmaḥ kṛtam evaṃ bhaviṣyati
english: And whatever other priests versed in the serpent sacrifice shall serve as his officiants — we shall bite them all; thus the deed will be accomplished.

sanskrit: tatrāpare 'mantrayanta dharmātmāno bhujaṃgamāḥ abuddhir eṣā yuṣmākaṃ brahmahatyā na śobhanā
english: Then other serpents of righteous soul deliberated there: "This is foolishness on your part — the slaying of a brahmin is not a thing of merit."

sanskrit: samyak saddharmamūlā hi vyasane śāntir uttamā adharmottaratā nāma kṛtsnaṃ vyāpādayej jagat
english: "For calm in adversity, rooted properly in right conduct, is the highest good; but dominance of unrighteousness would destroy the entire world."

sanskrit: apare tv abruvan nāgāḥ samiddhaṃ jātavedasam varṣair nirvāpayiṣyāmo meghā bhūtvā savidyutaḥ
english: Other serpents then said: "Becoming clouds with lightning, we shall quench the blazing sacrificial fire with rain."

sanskrit: srugbhāṇḍaṃ niśi gatvā vā apare bhujagottamāḥ pramattānāṃ harantv āśu vighna evaṃ bhaviṣyati
english: "Or let other excellent serpents go by night and swiftly steal the ladles and sacrificial vessels from the heedless attendants — thus the obstruction will be accomplished."

sanskrit: yajñe vā bhujagās tasmiñ śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ janaṃ daśantu vai sarvam evaṃ trāso bhaviṣyati
english: "Or let serpents at that sacrifice, in hundreds and thousands, bite all the people — thus terror will come about."

sanskrit: athavā saṃskṛtaṃ bhojyaṃ dūṣayantu bhujaṃgamāḥ svena mūtrapurīṣeṇa sarvabhojyavināśinā
english: "Or let the serpents defile the prepared food with their own urine and excrement, destroying all the food."

sanskrit: apare tv abruvaṃs tatra ṛtvijo 'sya bhavāmahe yajñavighnaṃ kariṣyāmo dīyatāṃ dakṣiṇā iti vaśyatāṃ ca gato 'sau naḥ kariṣyati yathepṣitam
english: Others said there: "Let us become his priests; we will obstruct the sacrifice — let fees be given." And having come under our sway, he will act as we desire.

sanskrit: apare tv abruvaṃs tatra jale prakrīḍitaṃ nṛpam gṛham ānīya badhnīmaḥ kratur evaṃ bhaven na saḥ
english: Others said there: "Let us seize the king while he is sporting in the water, bring him home, and bind him — thus the rite shall not take place."

sanskrit: apare tv abruvaṃs tatra nāgāḥ sukṛtakāriṇaḥ daśāmainaṃ pragṛhyāśu kṛtam evaṃ bhaviṣyati chinnaṃ mūlam anarthānāṃ mṛte tasmin bhaviṣyati
english: Other serpents who were doers of good deeds said there: "Let us quickly seize and bite him — thus the deed will be accomplished. When he is dead, the root of our misfortunes will be severed."

sanskrit: eṣā vai naiṣṭhikī buddhiḥ sarveṣām eva saṃmatā yathā vā manyase rājaṃs tat kṣipraṃ saṃvidhīyatām
english: "This indeed is the final counsel agreed upon by all; or as you, O lord, may think best — let that be arranged quickly."

sanskrit: ity uktvā samudaikṣanta vāsukiṃ pannageśvaram vāsukiś cāpi saṃcintya tān uvāca bhujaṃgamān
english: Having spoken thus, they all looked toward Vāsuki, the lord of serpents; and Vāsuki too, having reflected, spoke to those serpents.

sanskrit: naiṣā vo naiṣṭhikī buddhir matā kartuṃ bhujaṃgamāḥ sarveṣām eva me buddhiḥ pannagānāṃ na rocate
english: "This final counsel of yours is not what I consider should be done, O serpents; none of these plans of all the serpents pleases me."

sanskrit: kiṃ tv atra saṃvidhātavyaṃ bhavatāṃ yad bhaved dhitam anenāhaṃ bhṛśaṃ tapye guṇadoṣau madāśrayau
english: "But what is to be arranged here for the benefit of all of you — I am greatly tormented by this, since both the merits and the defects rest with me."

sanskrit: sūta uvāca śrutvā tu vacanaṃ teṣāṃ sarveṣām iti ceti ca vāsukeś ca vacaḥ śrutvā elāpatro 'bravīd idam
english: The Sūta said: Having heard the words of all of them — the various proposals — and having heard the speech of Vāsuki, Elāpatra spoke thus.

sanskrit: na sa yajño na bhavitā na sa rājā tathāvidhaḥ janamejayaḥ pāṇḍaveyo yato 'smākaṃ mahābhayam
english: "That sacrifice will not fail to take place; nor will that king be otherwise — Janamejaya the Pāṇḍava descendant, from whom comes our great fear."

sanskrit: daivenopahato rājan yo bhaved iha pūruṣaḥ sa daivam evāśrayate nānyat tatra parāyaṇam
english: "A man who is struck by fate, O king, must take shelter in fate alone — there is no other recourse in that matter."

sanskrit: tad idaṃ daivam asmākaṃ bhayaṃ pannagasattamāḥ daivam evāśrayāmo 'tra śṛṇudhvaṃ ca vaco mama
english: "This fear of ours is thus from fate, O best of serpents; let us take shelter in fate alone in this matter — and hear my words."

sanskrit: ahaṃ śāpe samutsṛṣṭe samaśrauṣaṃ vacas tadā mātur utsaṅgam ārūḍho bhayāt pannagasattamāḥ
english: "When the curse was being uttered, I heard those words at that time, seated in fear on our mother's lap, O best of serpents."

sanskrit: devānāṃ pannagaśreṣṭhās tīkṣṇās tīkṣṇā iti prabho pitāmaham upāgamya duḥkhārtānāṃ mahādyute
english: "O best among serpents, O lord of great splendor, the gods, afflicted with grief, approached the Grandfather, saying 'The fierce ones, the fierce ones!'"

sanskrit: devā ūcuḥ kā hi labdhvā priyān putrāñ śaped evaṃ pitāmaha ṛte kadrūṃ tīkṣṇarūpāṃ devadeva tavāgrataḥ
english: The gods said: "Who indeed, having obtained beloved sons, would curse them thus, O Grandfather, except Kadrū of fierce nature — before you, O god of gods?"

sanskrit: tatheti ca vacas tasyās tvayāpy uktaṃ pitāmaha etad icchāma vijñātuṃ kāraṇaṃ yan na vāritā
english: "And you too uttered the words 'So be it' to her speech, O Grandfather — this we wish to understand: what is the reason why she was not restrained?"

sanskrit: brahmovāca bahavaḥ pannagās tīkṣṇā bhīmavīryā viṣolbaṇāḥ prajānāṃ hitakāmo 'haṃ na nivāritavāṃs tadā
english: Brahman said: "Many serpents are fierce, of terrible might, and overflowing with venom; wishing for the welfare of living beings, I did not restrain her at that time."

sanskrit: ye dandaśūkāḥ kṣudrāś ca pāpacārā viṣolbaṇāḥ teṣāṃ vināśo bhavitā na tu ye dharmacāriṇaḥ
english: "Those that bite, the vile ones that walk in evil and overflow with venom — their destruction will come; but not those who walk in righteousness."

sanskrit: yannimittaṃ ca bhavitā mokṣas teṣāṃ mahābhayāt pannagānāṃ nibodhadhvaṃ tasmin kāle tathāgate
english: "And the reason for the deliverance of those serpents from that great fear — hear that now, when the time has come."

sanskrit: yāyāvarakule dhīmān bhaviṣyati mahān ṛṣiḥ jaratkārur iti khyātas tejasvī niyatendriyaḥ
english: "In the clan of the Yāyāvaras, a great wise sage shall arise, famed as Jaratkāru, of brilliant energy, with subdued senses."

sanskrit: tasya putro jaratkāror utpatsyati mahātapāḥ āstīko nāma yajñaṃ sa pratiṣetsyati taṃ tadā tatra mokṣyanti bhujagā ye bhaviṣyanti dhārmikāḥ
english: "His son, born of Jaratkāru, of great austerity, named Āstīka, shall stop that sacrifice at that time; and there the serpents who shall be righteous will be released."

sanskrit: devā ūcuḥ sa munipravaro deva jaratkārur mahātapāḥ kasyāṃ putraṃ mahātmānaṃ janayiṣyati vīryavān
english: The gods said: "That chief of sages, O god, Jaratkāru of great austerity — upon whom shall that mighty one, valiant in power, beget his great-souled son?"

sanskrit: brahmovāca sanāmāyāṃ sanāmā sa kanyāyāṃ dvijasattamaḥ apatyaṃ vīryavān devā vīryavaj janayiṣyati
english: Brahman said: "Upon a maiden of the same name as himself, O gods — that best of twice-born, that mighty one, shall beget an offspring equal in valor."

sanskrit: elāpatra uvāca evam astv iti taṃ devāḥ pitāmaham athābruvan uktvā caivaṃ gatā devāḥ sa ca devaḥ pitāmahaḥ
english: Elāpatra said: "'So be it,' the gods said to that Grandfather; and having spoken thus, the gods departed, and so did that divine Grandfather."

sanskrit: so 'ham evaṃ prapaśyāmi vāsuke bhaginīṃ tava jaratkārur iti khyātāṃ tāṃ tasmai pratipādaya
english: "I thus foresee this, O Vāsuki: your sister who is known as Jaratkāru — give her to him."

sanskrit: bhaikṣavad bhikṣamāṇāya nāgānāṃ bhayaśāntaye ṛṣaye suvratāya tvam eṣa mokṣaḥ śruto mayā
english: "To the sage of holy vows who will come begging like a mendicant, give her for the pacification of the serpents' fear — this deliverance I heard of."

sanskrit: sūta uvāca elāpatrasya tu vacaḥ śrutvā nāgā dvijottama sarve prahṛṣṭamanasaḥ sādhu sādhv ity apūjayan
english: The Sūta said: O best of twice-born, having heard the words of Elāpatra, all the serpents, with rejoicing hearts, honored him saying "Well said, well said!"

sanskrit: tataḥ prabhṛti tāṃ kanyāṃ vāsukiḥ paryarakṣata jaratkāruṃ svasāraṃ vai paraṃ harṣam avāpa ca
english: From that time forward Vāsuki carefully guarded that maiden Jaratkāru, his sister; and he experienced the greatest joy.

sanskrit: tato nātimahān kālaḥ samatīta ivābhavat atha devāsurāḥ sarve mamanthur varuṇālayam
english: Then no very great time seemed to pass before all the gods and asuras churned the ocean, the abode of Varuṇa.

sanskrit: tatra netram abhūn nāgo vāsukir balināṃ varaḥ samāpyaiva ca tat karma pitāmaham upāgaman
english: There the serpent Vāsuki, best among the mighty, served as the rope; and having completed that labor, they approached the Grandfather.

sanskrit: devā vāsukinā sārdhaṃ pitāmaham athābruvan bhagavañ śāpabhīto 'yaṃ vāsukis tapyate bhṛśam
english: The gods together with Vāsuki then said to the Grandfather: "O blessed one, this Vāsuki, afraid of the curse, is greatly tormented."

sanskrit: tasyedaṃ mānasaṃ śalyaṃ samuddhartuṃ tvam arhasi jananyāḥ śāpajaṃ deva jñātīnāṃ hitakāṅkṣiṇaḥ
english: "You should remove this mental anguish arising from his mother's curse, O god — he who desires the welfare of his kinsmen."

sanskrit: hito hy ayaṃ sadāsmākaṃ priyakārī ca nāgarāṭ kuru prasādaṃ deveśa śamayāsya manojvaram
english: "For this king of serpents has always been helpful and dear to us; show your grace, O lord of gods, and quench the fever of his mind."

sanskrit: brahmovāca mayaivaitad vitīrṇaṃ vai vacanaṃ manasāmarāḥ elāpatreṇa nāgena yad asyābhihitaṃ purā
english: Brahman said: "That which was declared to him long ago by the serpent Elāpatra — that very word was dispensed by my own mind, O immortals."

sanskrit: tat karotv eṣa nāgendraḥ prāptakālaṃ vacas tathā vinaśiṣyanti ye pāpā na tu ye dharmacāriṇaḥ
english: "Let this lord of serpents carry out that word which has come to its appointed time; the evil ones will perish, but not those who walk in righteousness."

sanskrit: utpannaḥ sa jaratkārus tapasy ugre rato dvijaḥ tasyaiṣa bhaginīṃ kāle jaratkāruṃ prayacchatu
english: "That twice-born Jaratkāru, devoted to fierce austerity, has been born; let this one give him his sister Jaratkāru at the proper time."

sanskrit: yad elāpatreṇa vacas tadoktaṃ bhujagena ha pannagānāṃ hitaṃ devās tat tathā na tad anyathā
english: "What was spoken at that time by the serpent Elāpatra, O gods — that is for the benefit of the serpents; it is so and not otherwise."

sanskrit: sūta uvāca etac chrutvā sa nāgendraḥ pitāmahavacas tadā sarpān bahūñ jaratkārau nityayuktān samādadhat
english: The Sūta said: Hearing these words of the Grandfather, that lord of serpents then stationed many serpents, always engaged, to watch over Jaratkāru.

sanskrit: jaratkārur yadā bhāryām icched varayituṃ prabhuḥ śīghram etya mamākhyeyaṃ tan naḥ śreyo bhaviṣyati
english: "When the mighty Jaratkāru wishes to choose a wife, come quickly and inform me — that will be for our good."

sanskrit: śaunaka uvāca jaratkārur iti proktaṃ yat tvayā sūtanandana icchāmy etad ahaṃ tasya ṛṣeḥ śrotuṃ mahātmanaḥ
english: Śaunaka said: "O son of the Sūta, you have mentioned the name Jaratkāru — I wish to hear about that great-souled sage."

sanskrit: kiṃ kāraṇaṃ jaratkāror nāmaitat prathitaṃ bhuvi jaratkāruniruktaṃ tvaṃ yathāvad vaktum arhasi
english: "For what reason is this name Jaratkāru renowned on earth? You should properly explain the derivation of the name Jaratkāru."

sanskrit: sūta uvāca jareti kṣayam āhur vai dāruṇaṃ kārusaṃjñitam śarīraṃ kāru tasyāsīt tat sa dhīmāñ śanaiḥ śanaiḥ
english: The Sūta said: "'Jarā' they call a terrible wasting away; 'kāru' denotes the body — he had such a body; and that wise one, little by little,

sanskrit: kṣapayām āsa tīvreṇa tapasety ata ucyate jaratkārur iti brahman vāsuker bhaginī tathā
english: wore it away through fierce austerity — therefore he is called Jaratkāru, O brahmin; and likewise Vāsuki's sister."

sanskrit: evam uktas tu dharmātmā śaunakaḥ prāhasat tadā ugraśravasam āmantrya upapannam iti bruvan
english: Thus addressed, the righteous-souled Śaunaka laughed, and having acknowledged Ugraśravas, said "Well answered."

sanskrit: sūta uvāca atha kālasya mahataḥ sa muniḥ saṃśitavrataḥ tapasy abhirato dhīmān na dārān abhyakāṅkṣata
english: The Sūta said: Then, for a great length of time, that sage of sharpened vow, the wise one devoted to austerity, did not desire a wife.

sanskrit: sa ūrdhvaretās tapasi prasaktaḥ; svādhyāyavān vītabhayaklamaḥ san cacāra sarvāṃ pṛthivīṃ mahātmā; na cāpi dārān manasāpy akāṅkṣat
english: That great-souled one, practicing upward retention of seed, absorbed in austerity, devoted to sacred study, free from fear and weariness, wandered over the whole earth; and he did not desire a wife even in his mind.

sanskrit: tato 'parasmin saṃprāpte kāle kasmiṃś cid eva tu parikṣid iti vikhyāto rājā kauravavaṃśabhṛt
english: Then, at another time that arrived, there was a king renowned as Parīkṣit, the upholder of the Kaurava lineage.

sanskrit: yathā pāṇḍur mahābāhur dhanurdharavaro bhuvi babhūva mṛgayāśīlaḥ purāsya prapitāmahaḥ
english: Just as the mighty-armed Pāṇḍu, the foremost archer on earth, was fond of hunting — so was his great-grandfather of old.

sanskrit: mṛgān vidhyan varāhāṃś ca tarakṣūn mahiṣāṃs tathā anyāṃś ca vividhān vanyāṃś cacāra pṛthivīpatiḥ
english: Piercing deer, boars, hyenas, buffaloes, and other various forest creatures, that lord of the earth wandered about.

sanskrit: sa kadā cin mṛgaṃ viddhvā bāṇena nataparvaṇā pṛṣṭhato dhanur ādāya sasāra gahane vane
english: Once, having wounded a deer with a straight-jointed arrow, he gave chase into the dense forest, bow in hand.

sanskrit: yathā hi bhagavān rudro viddhvā yajñamṛgaṃ divi anvagacchad dhanuṣpāṇiḥ paryanveṣaṃs tatas tataḥ
english: Just as the blessed Rudra, having wounded the sacrifice-deer in the sky, followed after it with bow in hand, searching here and there.

sanskrit: na hi tena mṛgo viddho jīvan gacchati vai vanam pūrvarūpaṃ tu tan nūnam āsīt svargagatiṃ prati parikṣitas tasya rājño viddho yan naṣṭavān mṛgaḥ
english: For a deer once wounded by him does not go away alive into the forest; but this was surely a portent of his going to heaven — the deer that was wounded and vanished on that king Parīkṣit.

sanskrit: dūraṃ cāpahṛtas tena mṛgeṇa sa mahīpatiḥ pariśrāntaḥ pipāsārta āsasāda muniṃ vane
english: Led far away by that deer, that lord of the earth, exhausted and suffering from thirst, came upon a sage in the forest.

sanskrit: gavāṃ pracāreṣv āsīnaṃ vatsānāṃ mukhaniḥsṛtam bhūyiṣṭham upayuñjānaṃ phenam āpibatāṃ payaḥ
english: He was seated in the cow-pasture, largely consuming the foam flowing from the mouths of calves drinking milk.

sanskrit: tam abhidrutya vegena sa rājā saṃśitavratam apṛcchad dhanur udyamya taṃ muniṃ kṣucchramānvitaḥ
english: Running swiftly toward that sage of sharpened vow, the king, raising his bow and afflicted with hunger and fatigue, asked him.

sanskrit: bho bho brahmann ahaṃ rājā parikṣid abhimanyujaḥ mayā viddho mṛgo naṣṭaḥ kaccit tvaṃ dṛṣṭavān asi
english: "Ho there, O brahmin! I am the king Parīkṣit, son of Abhimanyu. A deer I wounded has gone missing — have you perhaps seen it?"

sanskrit: sa munis tasya novāca kiṃ cin maunavrate sthitaḥ tasya skandhe mṛtaṃ sarpaṃ kruddho rājā samāsajat
english: That sage, observing his vow of silence, said nothing at all to him; so the angry king placed a dead serpent on his shoulder with the tip of his bow.

sanskrit: dhanuṣkoṭyā samutkṣipya sa cainaṃ samudaikṣata na ca kiṃ cid uvācainaṃ śubhaṃ vā yadi vāśubham
english: Lifting it up with the tip of his bow, he looked at him, but spoke not a word to him — neither auspicious nor inauspicious.

sanskrit: sa rājā krodham utsṛjya vyathitas taṃ tathāgatam dṛṣṭvā jagāma nagaram ṛṣis tv āste tathaiva saḥ
english: That king, having cast off his anger, and distressed at seeing him in that condition, went to the city; the sage remained sitting just as he was.

sanskrit: taruṇas tasya putro 'bhūt tigmatejā mahātapāḥ śṛṅgī nāma mahākrodho duṣprasādo mahāvrataḥ
english: He had a young son of sharp energy and great austerity, named Śṛṅgī, of great wrath, hard to appease, and of mighty vows.

sanskrit: sa devaṃ param īśānaṃ sarvabhūtahite ratam brahmāṇam upatasthe vai kāle kāle susaṃyataḥ sa tena samanujñāto brahmaṇā gṛham eyivān
english: He regularly attended upon the supreme lord Brahman, the divine one devoted to the welfare of all beings, with complete self-restraint; and having been given leave by that Brahman, he went home.

sanskrit: sakhyoktaḥ krīḍamānena sa tatra hasatā kila saṃrambhī kopano 'tīva viṣakalpa ṛṣeḥ sutaḥ ṛṣiputreṇa narmārthaṃ kṛśena dvijasattama
english: O best of twice-born, as he was coming, he was addressed in jest by a playful, laughing friend — the son of a sage named Kṛśa, who was extremely hot-tempered, wrathful, and like venom, the sage's son.

sanskrit: tejasvinas tava pitā tathaiva ca tapasvinaḥ śavaṃ skandhena vahati mā śṛṅgin garvito bhava
english: "Your father, though so energetic and such an ascetic, carries a corpse on his shoulder — do not be so proud, O Śṛṅgī."

sanskrit: vyāharatsv ṛṣiputreṣu mā sma kiṃ cid vaco vadīḥ asmadvidheṣu siddheṣu brahmavitsu tapasviṣu
english: "Do not speak any such words to the sons of sages — to the accomplished ones, the knowers of Brahman, the ascetics such as we are."

sanskrit: kva te puruṣamānitvaṃ kva te vācas tathāvidhāḥ darpajāḥ pitaraṃ yas tvaṃ draṣṭā śavadharaṃ tathā
english: "Where is your self-importance now? Where are such words of yours, born of arrogance — you whose father you shall see carrying a corpse like that?"

sanskrit: sūta uvāca evam uktaḥ sa tejasvī śṛṅgī kopasamanvitaḥ mṛtadhāraṃ guruṃ śrutvā paryatapyata manyunā
english: The Sūta said: Thus addressed, that energetic Śṛṅgī, filled with anger, hearing that his teacher was carrying a dead thing, was consumed with fury.

sanskrit: sa taṃ kṛśam abhipreṣkya sūnṛtāṃ vācam utsṛjan apṛcchata kathaṃ tātaḥ sa me 'dya mṛtadhārakaḥ
english: Looking at that Kṛśa and suppressing a kind reply, he asked: "How is it that my father is today a carrier of a dead thing?"

sanskrit: kṛśa uvāca rājñā parikṣitā tāta mṛgayāṃ paridhāvatā avasaktaḥ pitus te 'dya mṛtaḥ skandhe bhujaṃgamaḥ
english: Kṛśa said: "Dear friend, the king Parīkṣit, while ranging about on a hunt, today hung a dead serpent on your father's shoulder."

sanskrit: śṛṅgy uvāca kiṃ me pitrā kṛtaṃ tasya rājño 'niṣṭaṃ durātmanaḥ brūhi tvaṃ kṛśa tattvena paśya me tapaso balam
english: Śṛṅgī said: "What wrong did my father do to that evil-souled king? Tell me truthfully, O Kṛśa — and witness the power of my austerity."
